key_insight: MemLens makes LLM memory management smarter by assigning value to interaction records instead of treating all memories equally. This helps agents keep useful information longer while filtering out redundant or low-impact data.
problem_solved: Existing LLM memory systems store heterogeneous interaction records in a coarse-grained way, which leads to memory bloat, redundancy, and poor long-horizon usefulness. The paper addresses the need for value-aware memory management for LLM-based agents.
method: Introduces a value-aware memory management system that estimates the usefulness of stored interaction records.
Uses interactive analytics to help inspect, understand, and manage memory contents more effectively.
Prioritizes high-impact memories and reduces the retention of redundant or low-value records.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, MemLens can improve long-term agent performance, personalization, and knowledge reuse by keeping memory repositories cleaner and more relevant. It also offers better visibility into how memory is managed, which can help with debugging and system optimization.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing user interactions flowing into memory, then being scored by value and stored or discarded
Before-vs-after comparison of coarse-grained memory vs value-aware memory
Scatter plot or bar chart of memory records ranked by utility/value
Dashboard-style analytics panel with filters, retention, and memory usage icons
paper_title: MemLens: A Value-Aware Memory Management System with Interactive Analytics for LLM-based Agents
paper_authors: Shuyue Wei, Chang Liu, Zimu Zhou, Yongxin Tong, Lizhen Cui
